raw_response:
Alright, let me sit down and think about this year. I'm 58 now, been farming these fields for thirty years. My wife passed a few years back and the kids are working in the city — it's just me on these 40 mu. That's the hardest part. I'm not young anymore, and there's no one else in the house to help when things get busy.

**Splitting the land.** I've been running wheat-maize on most of my ground and keeping some cotton. Cotton is a headache — the picking alone takes weeks and I have to hire people three or four times through the fall. But cotton brings cash, and the price has been okay. This year I'm keeping cotton at 10 mu and putting 30 mu into wheat-maize double cropping. Last year I had 12 mu of cotton and I was worn out by November. Ten is enough.

**Wheat (30 mu, October planting).** I've been planting Jimai 22 for years, it does well on my ground. I save some seed but mostly buy fresh every two years. I'll plant early-to-mid October like always — around October 10 if the soil moisture is right. For fertilizer, I do what the extension guy told me years back and what I've refined from experience. Base fertilizer is compound 15-15-15, about 40 kg per mu before plowing. Then at jointing in March I topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. That gets me to around 16-17 kg N per mu total, which has been giving me 450-500 kg yield on good years. Irrigation — I always do the winter irrigation before freeze-up, then one at jointing, one at heading. Three times if the rains come, four if they don't. Well water is expensive, the meter doesn't lie, but you can't skip these.

**Maize (30 mu, June planting right after wheat).** Tight window — I've got to combine the wheat, clear the straw, and get the maize in within a week. I hire the combine and the no-till planter together, it's the only way solo. Zhengdan 958 variety, dependable. Fertilizer at planting with the planter, compound plus some urea, then I side-dress urea at the big bell stage. Around 15 kg N per mu total. Maize usually doesn't need as much irrigation as wheat in our area — summer rains carry it — but if July turns dry I'll irrigate once or twice. Herbicide right after planting is non-negotiable, the weeds will eat you alive otherwise.

**Cotton (10 mu, April planting).** This is the crop I'm scaling back on because of labor. Local variety seed, plant late April after soil warms. Cotton wants phosphorus and potassium more than heavy nitrogen — I do compound 15-15-15 base at about 30 kg per mu, then topdress urea at squaring, maybe 10 kg. Total N around 12-13 kg per mu. I spray for bollworm two or three times through summer. Need to hire pickers — usually neighbors' wives, I pay per kg picked. Two to three pickings September through October.

**Cash.** My budget is tight but not desperate. Maize and wheat together cost me maybe 350 yuan per mu in inputs, cotton closer to 500 with the pesticide and hired picking. I'll spend around 30,000 yuan total on inputs and hired labor before I see any grain money back. I always keep a few thousand in reserve in case the pump breaks or I need to hire more help.
